sources.title: Burton: named methodological resources and Said’s gender limit in Imperial Optics (2011)
sources.citation: Antoinette Burton, “Introduction. Imperial Optics: Empire Histories, Interpretive Methods,” in Empire in Question: Reading, Writing, and Teaching British Imperialism (Duke University Press, 2011), selected pp. 4–7, 10, 12–14, 16–19.

verification.note: Fresh selected primary reading of Burton’s own introduction, principally printed pp. 4–7, 10, 12–14 and 16–19, in the 42-page publisher preview; visually collated pp. 4, 6, 10, 12 and 14. Title/copyright confirm 2011. Mrinalini Sinha authors the separate foreword and C. A. Bayly the separate afterword; neither is silently attributed to Burton. The preview ends at printed p. 19: remainder of introduction, endnotes and complete volume not read. Specific original works invoked by Burton were not freshly read. Exact page-local argument supports each proposed resource or criticism; institutional proximity and generic thanks do not. Original note-source identification beyond visible prose is not asserted. Publisher metadata also checked at https://www.dukeupress.edu/empire-in-question.

sources.title: Burton: specific criticism of Cannadine’s imperial interdependence account (2002 opening)
sources.citation: Antoinette Burton, “Déjà Vu All Over Again,” Journal of Colonialism and Colonial History 3, no. 1 (Spring 2002), doi:10.1353/cch.2002.0004. Selected substantive opening reproduced on ResearchGate; original journal landing page https://muse.jhu.edu/article/7422.

verification.note: Freshly read the third-party reproduced authorial opening under Abstract, including the novelty/interdependence discussion and specified Sinha/Hall criticism. This is actual substantive critical prose with named targets, not metadata alone. The reproduction also credits Cannadine’s citations and Philip Morgan’s interconnected model. Original publisher body presents an access challenge; complete article and original facsimile not checked, and no exact journal page/paragraph numbering asserted. Cannadine’s original book and cited Sinha/Hall originals not freshly read. The preview of Burton’s 2011 collection lists a reprint of the 2002 essay at p. 68; it does not supply that chapter body.
